PullRequest.Title: sessions: open exactly the dragged chat when moving a chat tab to a window
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #347005

Dragging a session's main chat tab out of the window opened the nested chat when the nested chat's tab was selected. The main chat's resource is the session resource, which the chat window provider resolves to the chat the session currently shows. `openChatInWindow` now passes `exactChat` whenever a chat is given, so exactly that chat opens. Opening a session (no chat given) still opens the chat it shows.

How to test:
- Open a session with a nested chat, choose `...` > Show Chat Tabs > Multiple, and select the nested chat's tab.
- Drag the main chat's tab out of the window: the new window shows the main chat.
- Dragging the nested chat's tab and Open in New Window on a session behave as before.

Validation:
- Added a unit test in `chatWindowContribution.test.ts`; it failed before the change and passes now.
- chatWindow test folders pass in Electron and Chromium; typecheck, eslint and valid-layers-check pass.
- Live check is partial: the before/after drag-out was a synthetic `dragstart`/`dragend` through CDP with the cursor-in-window check bypassed, since CDP cannot produce a native drag outside the window. A real mouse drag-out was not exercised.

Scenarios.Scenario: Detach or explicitly open a specific chat, including a session's main chat addressed by the session URI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command/drag path calls openChatInWindow, synchronously resolves current session/editor ownership, then awaits IChatWindowService.open. A cold canonical chat proceeds through provider resolution and auxiliary-window creation before the operation completes; an already-open canonical chat is only revealed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and initialize an auxiliary chat window and its editor parts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one for a cold explicit open whose canonical chat is not already shown; zero on a warm reveal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same open path could create one auxiliary window, but a session URI defaulted to the session's currently shown chat; the diff intentionally selects the main chat when the caller supplied that URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Window creation and editor-part initialization are awaited before the explicit open completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register the auxiliary window with the Electron host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC invocation only when a new native auxiliary window is created; zero when revealing an existing window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cold chat-window creation already performed the same single registration IPC.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user-selected chat. Provider lookup scans loaded sessions/chats (effective cardinality is the number of loaded sessions and their chats), as before; no loop over selected items is introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Opens for the same requested URI are serialized by SequencerByKey; different chats can open concurrently, unchanged. This diff changes only the exact/default in-flight coalescing key for explicit chats, not aggregate scheduling, and serialized follow-up resolution is bounded to the competing user actions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Open windows act as the positive cache. The service first checks the requested URI and, after provider resolution, checks the canonical chat, so warm opens reveal the existing window. exactChat changes which canonical chat a session URI resolves to but does not bypass the canonical deduplication check. Concurrent exact/default requests have different in-flight keys, but the per-requested-URI sequencer still serializes them and the post-resolution canonical check prevents a second window.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed option, provider branch, per-key sequencing, canonical deduplication, and native auxiliary-window boundary were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of loaded chats and native window-open duration vary, but the diff neither increases lookup multiplicity nor adds boundary fan-out. It can intentionally create the main-chat window where the previous incorrect resolution revealed a nested chat, which is bounded required work for the requested operation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added exactChat flag changes the requested canonical chat; any bounded extra window work is the intended result of opening the exact chat, with no repeated or scaling boundary work introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a session without specifying a chat, including opening a picked session in an existing chat window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: openChatInWindow derives the session's currently shown chat, passes exactChat false, and awaits IChatWindowService.open. In an existing target window it resolves the chat and opens/reveals its editor; otherwise it may create one auxiliary window.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optionally create an auxiliary window, or open one chat editor in the supplied existing window
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One window/editor operation for the single selected session; zero new windows when the canonical chat already shows or a target window is supplied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical: callers without a chat passed no exactChat option and resolved the session to its shown chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The open/reveal is awaited by the picker or command.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register a newly created native auxiliary window
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for an existing target/window reveal; one only for a cold new native window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same conditional IPC occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited only on the cold new-window path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One picked session per command. Session-pane lookup and provider resolution scale with loaded panes/sessions/chats exactly as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Same-URI requests remain serialized and coalesced under the default in-flight key. Different selected sessions retain the pre-existing independent concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The currently shown chat is selected before the service call. Existing chat windows are checked before and after canonical resolution; warm opens reveal rather than recreate. No new cache key or negative-cache behavior applies because exactChat remains false.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all no-chat callers and the option value were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Loaded-session count and editor initialization cost vary, but the changed line evaluates to false in this scenario and preserves the prior path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance change for session opens; the changed option explicitly preserves default resolution.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an explicit nested chat as a tab in or beside an existing chat window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The explicit chat URI reaches IChatWindowService.open with exactChat true. The service resolves the target in memory, checks whether its canonical chat already shows, and otherwise opens one editor in the existing window. No auxiliary window creation is needed when the supplied target remains valid.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicit chat and one target window per user action; lookup scans loaded chats/windows with unchanged cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Same requested URI is serialized; separate chat URIs remain independent as before. No loop or burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An existing canonical chat is revealed. A missing chat is resolved once and adopted by the target window; subsequent opens hit the open-window lookup. There is no negative-cache change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the target-window branch and provider exact-chat branch were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Editor rendering cost depends on chat contents, but exactChat only selects identity and does not change rendering frequency, retained history, or serialization volume.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff avoids resolving a session-named main chat to a selected nested chat and performs only the single editor operation requested.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and traced explicit-chat, session-open, drag/detach, picker, provider resolution, coalescing, canonical deduplication, editor movement, auxiliary-window creation, and native IPC paths. The change is a bounded identity-selection correction and introduces no actionable performance regression.
